_contract: Inputs for a CUDA engineering check of the migrated initialization code. This is ENGINEERING validation, not science: it answers 'do the operators execute on a real device without a placement or dtype error', and nothing about model quality. It produces no result, ranks nothing, and every artifact it writes is disposable. AUTHORIZES NOTHING.

model._why_a_fixture: A tiny randomly-initialized model, built from a config rather than downloaded. The defects this looks for are about WHERE tensors are and what dtype they carry, not how large they are, so a fixture exercises the same lines at a fraction of the load time and with no checkpoint dependency.
model._why_tied_embeddings: The real Qwen3 students tie the lm head to the embedding, and the operators rely on it: with an untied head the surgery guard correctly refuses, because lm_head.weight would be left holding random values. An untied fixture would therefore test a model this project does not build.

_why_two_geometries: One geometry can pass by accident when a shape happens to divide evenly. Two that differ in the dimensions the operators actually reshape -- depth, width, FFN and head grouping -- make a coincidence far less likely, and the directive asks for at least two.

target_geometries._why_this_grouping: 4 Q heads over 1 KV head: a valid GQA grouping that still differs from the parent's 4/2 and from `narrow`'s 2/1, so the head-grouping path is exercised at a second ratio. 3/3 was rejected by the operator because 4 parent Q heads do not group into 3 -- the refusal was correct and the geometry was wrong.

calibration._why_synthetic: Random token ids under a fixed seed. The real mixture is a licensed artifact and its content is irrelevant to a placement check; a synthetic batch keeps this runnable anywhere and makes the check reproducible from the config alone.

execution._device_is_not_negotiable: If CUDA is absent this reports NOT RUN. It must never fall back to CPU and report a pass, because CPU execution cannot observe the cross-device and dtype defects this exists to find.

run._roles_are_declared_by_the_caller: RunLayout holds no vocabulary of its own; these are this validation's roles and their paths inside the run.

_operator_ids_are_the_registered_ones: checked against aadistill.initialization.operators.base.registered_implementations(); an unknown id is refused before any device work, so a typo costs nothing rather than failing partway through a paid session
